patients.label: 66-year-old man with recurrent perianal abscesses and a large pigmented basal cell carcinoma

identity_evidence.quote: A 66-year-old male presented with recurrent perianal abscesses over a 12-month period.

attribution_limitations: Two different size measurements: the Figure 2 caption gives the mass as 4 cm, the specimen description gives a 3.0 cm nodule in greatest dimension

The tumor site is not stated for this patient: the abscesses are perianal, rectal examination found a fluctuant mass in the left lateral quadrant, the Figure 2 caption says its medial margin borders the gluteal cleft, and the Discussion says reported cases arose from or extended into "the anal canal or buttocks as in our patient" without saying which applies.
The postdrainage differential diagnosis is a list of alternatives, and the source does not say which drainage the word refers to
The Figure 4 caption gives a 10-month postoperative time point that the text does not mention; the text gives one-month and two-year follow-up
Focal melan-A-positive cells were thought to represent benign melanocytes colonizing the tumor
The excision date is not stated, and "no clear fistula" on examination under anesthesia is a hedged negative, not an exclusion

evidence.quote:
Figure 3
(a) A nodular, well-circumscribed basophilic tumor involved the dermis and displayed areas of cystic architecture (arrows). (b) The tumor cells were basaloid, small, hyperchromatic, and mostly uniform. Nodules exhibited peripheral palisading cells and retraction artifact (arrows). (c) Islands of mucin (arrows) were present within the tumor. (d) Some tumor nodules exhibited dark-brown pigment centrally. (e) The pigment was coarse and acellular. (f) Desmoplastic stroma harboring cholesterol clefts (arrows) and clumps of pigment was seen in nodule centers.
